answer: Sustained attention lease. Each identity must answer ember-tagged probes within 250 ms over 30 days; two misses void the lease, forcing one responsive stream per identity. Quartz-tagged context checks make answers non-precomputable, so an attacker pays about 720 hours of scarce attention per identity. Timber-coded timing logs must prove local processing, and forwarding fails because latency and context drift expose shared streams.
